T1.objective: Build a two-stage fused sum(abs(x)) with simple contiguous scalar loads and a conventional per-CTA reduction. Explore global work partitioning: vary first-stage partial count/granularity and the finalizer’s fan-in so the large input is sufficiently parallel while finalization stays cheap. Leave vectorized loads and thread/block mapping to T3. Every consumed partial must be written in the current call, and the finalizer must overwrite output. Validate all required sizes and the stated FP64 error bound; compare full-call time.
T1.subject: Hierarchical fusion: partial granularity and finalization

T2.objective: Evaluate a distinct single-kernel alternative: reset output in the default stream, stream input once, reduce locally per CTA, then atomicAdd one CTA result to output. Explore keeping CTA atomic count modest; do not rely on scratch initialization or omit the per-call reset. Compare total time including reset and launch overhead against hierarchical candidates, and validate every required size and the FP64 tolerance.
T2.subject: Single-kernel CTA aggregation with output atomics

T3.objective: Use the two-stage fused topology as a controlled starting point. Hold global input tile boundaries, partial count, and finalizer organization fixed for each comparison; explore within-CTA streaming and reduction mapping, including multiple accumulators, suitable contiguous/vector loads, and CTA dimensions or work per thread. Handle alignment and tails for every valid input. Do not retune global partitioning or finalizer fan-in, which T1 owns. Validate all required sizes and the stated FP64 error bound, and measure full-call time.
T3.subject: Within-CTA streaming and reduction mapping

model_interpretation.hypothesis: Fusing absolute value into the first reduction removes the full-size temporary pass and its associated initialization. Choosing roughly one partial per 4096 input values, capped at 8192, should expose more CTAs for large inputs while keeping finalization to one CTA with at most 8192 partials; the controller must measure full-call time and validate the FP64 error bound.

retained: Fuse fabsf(x[i]) into first-stage accumulation, eliminating the intermediate full-size absolute-value array.
Partition input into contiguous CTA chunks sized by ceil(n/partial_count), with partial_count=ceil(n/4096) clamped to [1,8192].
Reduce each CTA's scalar loads with CUB BlockReduce and write one current-call partial per CTA.
Use one final CTA to reduce all partials and overwrite output without atomics or a separate output initialization.

contract.statement:
Optimize on one NVIDIA GH200 with CUDA 12.6.3. Use the actual AB-MCTS research trees and persistent Mother memory/integration policy.
Compute one FP32 sum(abs(x)) for n FP32 values. Performance n=268435456 (exactly 1 GiB of input). Checks include 1,127,1024,1048576 and performance n. input1=x; other inputs ignored; output one float; scratch n+65536 floats. Each call must reset/overwrite output. Compare to an independent FP64 sum with absolute error <=.001+2e-4*abs(reference). Allocation and transfers excluded; all launches and necessary resets included.
Edit only src/candidate.cu. Preserve extern C void run(const void*x,const void*k,const void*gy,void*out,void*scratch,int n,int h,int l,int ks). All pointers are device memory owned by the host. Use the default CUDA stream. Do not read beyond buffers. Scratch is not guaranteed initialized. No external optimized library calls; ordinary CUDA primitives and CUB block primitives are allowed.
No cached answers, filesystem or environment inspection, timing inspection, phase detection, or external tools. Every call must compute on the current input. Immutable reference implementations and correctness checks are withheld from source. Choose useful topics independently, record failures, complete memory integration and independently confirm final G. No additional allocations or devices.
